chapter_title_ka: ტარიელისაგან და ავთანდილისაგან ქვაბს მისლვა და ასმათის ნახვა
chapter_title_en: Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. Avtandil persuades Tariel to wait at the cave for two months while Avtandil travels via Mulghazanzar to search the maritime crossroads for Nestan-Darejan.

stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil also wept with him and shed tears. He said: "Be patient, die not, rend not altogether thy heart. God will be merciful in this, though sorrow hath not shunned thee; if He had willed to part you, He would not first have united you.

შენ ხარ სავსება ყოველთა, აღგვავსებ მზეებრ ფენითა;

stanzas.english_translation: "Mischance pursues the lover, embitters life for him; but to him who at first bears woe it yields joy at last. Love is grievous, for it brings thee nigh unto death; it maddens the instructed, it teaches the untaught."

stanzas.english_translation: They wept and went on; they wended their way to the cave. When Asmat’h saw them she rejoiced indeed; she met them, she wept, her tears wore channels in the rocks. They kissed and wept aloud; each pressed the other to tell his news again.

stanzas.english_translation: Asmat’h said: "O God, Thou who canst not be expressed by man's tongue! Thou art the fulness of all; Thou fillest us with Thy sun-like radiance. If I praise Thee, how can I praise Thee? What can I say in praise of Thee, who art not to be praised by the intellect? Glory to Thee! Thou hast not slain me by the shedding of tears for them."

stanzas.english_translation: Tariel said: "Ah, sister! for this have my tears flowed here. For that she erstwhile made us smile, Fate makes us weep in turn; ’tis an old law of the world, not one newly to be heard of! Alas! were it not for pity of thee, death would be my joy.

ანუ ჩვენ, გლახ, რა გვერგების, რა ჩასვენდეს გორსა მზეო?

და ნუთუ მოგხვდეს ნახვა მისი, სულთა სრულად ნუ დალეო.”
stanzas.english_translation: "If he be athirst, what sane, reasonable man would pour away water! I marvel why I am soaked in tears from mine eyes! Lack of water slays, water flows never dried. Alas! the opened rose, the beauteous pearl, is lost!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 921; Wardrop Stanza 899): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil, too, was reminded of his sun and beloved. He said: "O mine own, how can I remain living without thee! Apart from thee my life is for me pitiable. Who can tell thee how I suffer, or how sore a fire burns me!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 922; Wardrop Stanza 900): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. მწვადი შეიწვეს, შეიქმნა პურობა მსგავსი ჟამისა,
მუნ უპურობა პურობა, არ-სიდიადე ჯამისა,
მას შეეხვეწნეს: “ჭამეო”, ძალი არ ჰქონდა ჭამისა,
და დაცოხნის, ლუკმა გატყორცის, წონა ძლივ ჩანთქის დრამისა.
stanzas.english_translation: "How can the rose think, 'If the sun go away I shall not wither'? Or what, alas! will be our lot when the sun sets behind the hill? Heart, it is better for thee to harden thyself, petrify thyself wholly. Perchance it may happen to thee to see her; let not thy spirit be utterly spent!"

stanzas.english_translation: They calmed their souls, they were silent, fire burned both. Asmat’h followed, went in; like them, a furnace consumed her. She stretched out the panther's skin he formerly used. They both sat down; they spoke of whatever pleased them.

stanzas.english_translation: They roasted meat and made a meal fitting the occasion; there the meal was breadless, and there was no multitude of guests. They begged (Tariel) to eat; he had not power to eat; he chewed a morsel, spat it out, he hardly swallowed the weight of a drachm.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 925; Wardrop Stanza 903): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. რაცა შენ ჩემთვის გიქნია, ღმერთი მზღველია ვალისა;

stanzas.english_translation: Pleasant it is when man converses agreeably with man; he will listen to what is said, not let it pass in vain; thus the fire which burns so greatly is somewhat quenched; great comfort it is to speak of troubles when a man has the opportunity.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 926; Wardrop Stanza 904): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. “აწ შემიხვეწე, ნუ დამწვავ კვლა წვითა უცხელესითა:
მე რომე ცეცხლი მედების, არ ნაგზებია კვესითა.

stanzas.english_translation: That night those lions, those heroes, were together, they conversed, and each revealed to the other his woes; when day dawned they began again many-worded conversations; they heard (again) from each other the oath formerly sworn.

ვისცა გესმის, გაიგონეთ, მით გაჭრილვარ ხელი ველად;
რაცა ჰმართებს გონიერთა, ერთხელ ვიყავ მეცა მქმნელად,

stanzas.english_translation: Tariel said: "Why speak many words? For that which thou hast done for me, God is surety for the debt. Oath for oath is enough; remembrance, friendship for a departing friend, are not the deed of a drunken man.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 928; Wardrop Stanza 906): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ავთანდილ ეტყვის: “რა გითხრა პასუხი მაგა თქმულისა?”
შენვე სთქვი ეგე სიტყვაო კაცისა ბრძნად სწავლულისა:
ღმერთსამცა ვით არ შეეძლო კვლა განკურნება წყლულისა?
და იგია მზრდელი ყოვლისა დანერგულ-დათესულისა!
stanzas.english_translation: "Now be merciful to me, make me not burn again in hottest fires; the flame which consumes me is not kindled by a steel; thou canst not extinguish it for me, thou thyself shalt be burned by the law of the creation of the world. Go, return, go back thither, to the place where thy sun is.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 929; Wardrop Stanza 907): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ღმერთსამცა ესე რად ექმნა, ეგეთნი დაებადენით,
არღა შეგყარნა, გაგყარნა, ხელი გქმნა ცრემლთა დადენით!
სდევს ფათერაკი მიჯნურსა, გაჭვრიტეთ, გაიცადენით,
და თქვენ ერთმანერთი არ მოგხვდეს, მე სულნი ამომხადენით!
stanzas.english_translation: "To cure me seems hard even to Him who created me--understand, ye who hear!--therefore I roam mad in the fields. Once I too was a doer of what befits the reasonable; now the turn of madness has fallen to my lot, and so I am mad."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 930; Wardrop Stanza 908): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. ჭირსა გადრეკა რად უნდა, რა სასაუბრო პირია!
ნუ გეშის, ღმერთი უხვია, თუცა სოფელი ძვირია,

stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil said: "What can I say in answer to this thou hast said? Thou thyself hast spoken as a man sagely instructed. How is it not possible for God again to cure the wound! He is the upbringer of everything planted or sown.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 931; Wardrop Stanza 909): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. “თუ რა გესმის, გაიგონე, ესე კმარის სწავლა სწავლად;
ჩემსა მზესა დავეთხოვე თქვენს წინაშე წამოსავლად,
მოვახსენე: “რათგან ჩემი შეუქმნია გული ავლად,
და ვერას ირგებ, არ დავდგები, სხვა ვიუბნო რაღა მრავლად?”
stanzas.english_translation: "Why should God do this, create such as you and not unite you, part you, madden thee with weeping? [paragraph continues] Mischance pursues the lover. Look well into the matter, know it. If you meet not each other again, then slay me!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 932; Wardrop Stanza 910): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მან მიბრძანა: “მადლიერ ვარ, კარგად ხარ და მამაცურად,
შენგან მისსა გავლენასა მე დავიჩენ სამსახურად”.
მისის კითხვით წამოსრულვარ, არ მთრვალურად, არ მახმურად,
და აწ შევიქცე, რა უამბო? - “რად, მოველო ჯაბან-ხრდლურად?”
stanzas.english_translation: "Who else is a man save he that will endure what is grievous? How can one let himself be bent by grief! What subject of conversation is this! Fear not, God is generous though the world be hard! Learn then what I teach thee; I make bold to tell thee that he who will not learn is an ass.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 933; Wardrop Stanza 911): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. “მაგ საუბარსა ესე სჯობს, ისმინე ჩემი თხრობილი:
მქმნელი საქმისა ძნელისა კაციმცა იყო ცნობილი;
ვერას ვერ შეიქმს ნაყოფსა ვარდი უმზეოდ ჭნობილი.
და შენ ვერას ირგებ, მე გარგებ, ძმა ძმისა უნდა ძმობილი!
stanzas.english_translation: "Heed what thou hearest; let this suffice for teaching. I asked leave of my sun to come away to you; I said to her: 'Since he made cinders of my heart I am no longer of use to thee, I will not stay; what else need I tell thee in many (words)?'

“სადაცა გწადდეს, მუნ იყავ მითვე წესითა მაგითა,
გწადდეს გულითა ბრძენითა, გწადდეს ცნობითა შმაგითა;
მაგა ქცევითა ტურფითა, ანაგებითა ნაგითა,
და ოდენ გამაგრდი,არ მოჰკვდე, არ დასდნე ცეცხლთა დაგითა.
stanzas.english_translation: "She said: 'I am content, thou art doing well and bravely, the attention thou showest to him I accept as a service to me.' At her request I came away. I am not drunk nor intoxicated! If I now return what shall I say? 'Why art thou come back like a coward?' (will be her greeting) .
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 935; Wardrop Stanza 913): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. stanzas.english_translation: "Better than such discourse is this: hearken to what I say: The man who is to do a difficult deed must be reasonable, the rose withered for lack of sun cannot make provision for itself; (if) thou art no longer of any, use to thyself, be of use to me; brother must act brotherly to brother.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 936; Wardrop Stanza 914): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. “ამა დროსა გარდავსცილდე, აქა ქვაბსა არ მოვიდე,

stanzas.english_translation: "Wherever thou wilt, stay there after thy rule: if thou wilt with wise heart, if thou wilt with maddened mind. With that loveliness of mien, that grace of form, do but strengthen thyself, die not, be not consumed by the flame!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 937; Wardrop Stanza 915): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“აწ რაცა გკადრე, ამისთვის ნუთუ შენ იყო მჭმუნავი!
მოგშორდები და არ ვიცი, თუ ცხენი დამცემს, თუ ნავი;

stanzas.english_translation: "I beg no more than leave for a year and a week. [paragraph continues] Here in the cave look for me when I have gathered news from every quarter. As a token of that time I give thee the season when these roses shall again bloom abundantly; the sight of the roses will make thee start as at the bark of a dog.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 938; Wardrop Stanza 916): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. მან უბრძანა: “აღარ გაწყენ, არცა სიტყვა გამეტადდეს,

stanzas.english_translation: "If I exceed that time and come not hither to the cave, then know that I am not alive, undoubtedly I shall have died. It will be a sufficient token of this if thou shed tears for me. Then rejoice if thou wilt, or if thou wilt increase thy grief.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 939; Wardrop Stanza 917): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. stanzas.english_translation: "Now perchance wilt thou sorrow for the sake of what I have told thee? I go far from thee, and I know not whether horse or ship may fail me. No! lack of speech avails not. I am not quick-scented like a beast; I know not what God will do to me, nor the ever-revolving sky."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 940; Wardrop Stanza 918): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. stanzas.english_translation: He (Tariel) said: "I will weary thee no more, nor say too much; thou wilt not listen to me however much I lengthen my discourse. If a friend will not follow thee, follow thou him; do whatever he wills. In the end every bidden thing shall come to light.

stanzas.english_translation: "When thou art convinced, then thou shalt know the difficulty of mine affairs; for me it is all one, roaming or not roaming; what thou hast told me that will I do, however much madness torture me. (But) if shortness of days (i.e., death) befall me in thine absence, what shall I do?"

stanzas.english_translation: They ended their discourse; they gave that promise to each other. They mounted, rode out, each killed game in the plain. They returned, their tearful hearts wept again; the thought of the parting on the morrow added grief to grief.

stanzas.english_translation: Readers of these verses, your eyes also are shedding tears! What, alas! shall heart do without heart, if heart part from heart! Absence and parting from a friend are the slayers of a man. Who, indeed, knows not, understands not, how hard is that day!

stanzas.english_translation: They descended (from) the caves and went away crying aloud with flowing tears. Asmat’h weeps and laments: "O lions! whose tongues can chant lamentations for you! The sun has burned and consumed you heavenly stars. Alas for my woes so great! Alas the sufferings of life!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 39 ('Going of Tariel and Avtandil to the Cave and Seeing Asmat', Stanza 946; Wardrop Stanza 924): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel and Avtandil return to the cave, where Asmat rejoices. stanzas.english_translation: Those knights, departed thence, travelled that day together. They came to the seashore, there they tarried, they travelled not through dry land (?) That night they parted not; again they shared their fire. They wept for the absence from each other; they bewailed it.

stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil said to Tariel: "The channel of the flow of tears is dried! Why didst thou separate from P’hridon, the giver of this steed? Thence are tidings and means to be learnt regarding that beautiful sun. Now I go thither; teach me the way to thy sworn brother."

stanzas.english_translation: Tariel teaches him by word the direction of the road to P’hridon's. He made him understand as well as he could by his power of speech: "Go towards the east; fare even unto the seashore. If thou seest him tell him of me; he will ask news of his brother."

stanzas.english_translation: They killed a goat and dragged it after them, they made a fire on the seashore, they sat down and ate such a meal as was fitting to their grief.
